review.notes:
Checked every one of the 114 entries in trng.json against neorv32_trng.vhd (lines 20-171 hold all occurrences; the rest of the file is the separate neoTRNG entity). Every entry's line_text matches the source line it claims, verified programmatically.

What I verified per tag family:
- DECL_PORT (25, 26, 27, 28) and DECL_SIGNAL (71 for enable/fifo_clr, 84 for fifo) are on the right statements; the component port clause at 62-67 correctly produced no entries.
- DECL_FIELD: all bus_req_i.* and bus_rsp_o.* say the record type is declared outside this source, and all fifo.* say it is declared in this source. grep confirms only `type fifo_t is record` (74-83) exists here; bus_req_t/bus_rsp_t come from a package.
- PROCESS_TRIG (90) / EDGE_CHECK (96) / IF_COND (92, 103, 104, 108, 114) are kept apart as CONFLICT_RULES requires.
- Targets: LHS_PROC inside process bus_access (93, 94, 95, 98, 99, 100, 101, 105, 106, 109, 110, 111, 112, 115, 117) and LHS_CONC for the two concurrent conditional assignments (170, 171). Every index inside a target is a named constant or a literal, so no INDEX entry is owed anywhere.
- Add-ons: bus_rsp_o.data gets INDEXED_NAME at 109, 111, 112 (one position) and PART_SELECT at 110, 115, 117 (a range), each with the range spelled out in the Role; bus_req_i.addr gets INDEXED_NAME at 108 and 171; bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c) / (ctrl_fifo_clr_c) on the right-hand side at 105/106 correctly carries INDEXED_NAME alone, per the DIRR_ASS exclusion "an index makes it INDEXED_NAME ... each written alone where no primary SITE matches".
- DIRR_ASS at 98, 109, 112, 117 each has a right-hand side that is exactly the element (no operator, index or range); no whole-right-hand-side slice occurs in this file, so the PART_SELECT-alone case never arises.
- FIELD_USE is written alone on every base occurrence (bus_req_i x9, bus_rsp_o x9, fifo x15) and each Role names the field reached; the three bus_req_i entries sharing line 171 are told apart by field (stb, rw, addr).
- WHEN_COND at 170 (enable, fifo_clr) and 171 (bus_req_i.stb, .rw, .addr) is never confused with WHEN_EXPR; the chosen and alternative expressions there are the literals '1' and '0', which are not elements.
- ASSOC_ACTUAL: all 15 actuals name their formal in the Role (clk_i, rstn_i, enable_i, valid_o, data_o, clear_i, half_o, wdata_i, we_i, free_o, re_i, rdata_o, avail_o).
- No Role holds a line number, and a regex sweep for purpose words (reset, clock, enable, default, valid, flag, clear, available, FIFO...) turned up only element names and formal names, which the project decisions allow.

Two borderline calls I deliberately did not report: (a) the FIELD_USE Roles on bus_rsp_o at 110, 115 and 117 add a parenthetical naming the part-select, but it is attached to "field 'data'", states a true syntactic fact about the field, and does not put PART_SELECT on the base; (b) the bus_req_i.data Roles at 105/106 open with "Right-hand side of a sequential signal assignment" but immediately say "written as an indexed name", so they do not claim the "whole right-hand side" position that DIRR_ASS would need.

review.notes: All 73 entries checked against the source lines 228-378 and the rulebook. Points deliberately not reported, with the reason: (1) cell_en_out id 5 (line 336) and sample_cnt id 9 (line 367) carry ATTR_PREFIX alone while sample_cnt id 4 (line 355) carries IF_COND + ATTR_PREFIX; this is consistent, because conflict rule 7 writes an add-on with "IF_COND inside an if or elsif condition" (a place, which the attribute prefix is in) but "RHS_OPERAND where an operator joins the occurrence to something else", which no operator does for an attribute prefix used as an index. (2) The slice targets and slice right-hand sides (cell_en_in id 4, cell_en_out id 3, sample_sreg id 5) follow conflict rule 7 and the PART_SELECT conflict rule as written. (3) debias_sreg id 7 and sample_cnt id 8 say "whole right-hand side ... no primary SITE matches" with INDEXED_NAME alone; that matches the DIRR_ASS exclusion "an index makes it INDEXED_NAME ... written alone where no primary SITE matches", so the phrase was not read as contradicting the tags. (4) Roles that say "in the if branch where rstn_i = '0'" name a condition, which is syntax, not purpose. (5) Every pair of occurrences sharing a line (334, 336, 341, 355, 359, 360, 367) is told apart by its Role. No Role holds a line number; the numbers present are bit ranges and indices, which the project decisions call code text.

verdicts.corrected_expected: SITE Tagged: ["LHS_CONC"]
verdicts.reason: Line 342 reads `debias_data  <= debias_sreg(0);` in the architecture body, outside every process block (the debiasing process ends at line 338). debias_data is the name on the left of <=, i.e. the assignment target, so the LHS_CONC trigger applies verbatim ("the target (left-hand side) of a signal assignment written outside any process block"). DIRR_ASS requires the element to be the whole right-hand side; the right-hand side here is debias_sreg(0), not debias_data, so DIRR_ASS cannot apply. The reviewer's quoted LHS_CONC trigger exists in the rulebook word for word.

verdicts.corrected_expected: Role: "target on the left of <= of a concurrent signal assignment (debias_data <= debias_sreg(0))"
verdicts.reason: The Role states debias_data is the "whole right-hand side" of the assignment on line 342, which the source contradicts: debias_data stands left of <= and debias_sreg(0) is the right-hand side. Section G requires the Role to give the element's position in the statement (target vs whole right-hand side) specifically enough that the SITE can be verified; the stated position is factually wrong. The quoted DIRR_ASS trigger ("no operator, no index, no range and no other name appears to the right of <=") exists in the rulebook and shows the element it describes is the RHS name, not this occurrence.

verdicts.corrected_expected: Role: "target on the left of <= of a sequential signal assignment (sample_sreg <= (others => '0')) in the inner if then branch"
verdicts.reason: Section G ends with "Do not say what a signal or a branch is for. Name only its syntax." — the quoted rule exists. The Role's parenthetical "(reset of sample_sreg)" states what the assignment is for, and "reset" is named in the owner decisions as a forbidden purpose word. Line 357 is `sample_sreg <= (others => '0');` inside the then branch of the inner if, so the syntax-only wording still tells this occurrence apart from id 2 on line 352.

verdicts.corrected_expected: Role: "operand in the right-hand side of a sequential signal assignment, joined by operator and" (unchanged; naming the immediate operator not is also acceptable)
verdicts.reason: Line 336 is `debias_state <= (not debias_state) and cell_en_out(cell_en_out'left);`. The occurrence is an operand on the right-hand side of a non-conditional sequential signal assignment, so RHS_OPERAND is right, and section G only requires the Role to give the statement and the element's position (operand) — no rule requires naming the operator at all, let alone the innermost one. The reviewer's "rule_quote" is only one of the forms listed under section F rule 10 (`<target_label> <= not <element_label>;`); it is a form example, not a requirement about Role wording. The right-hand side is an and expression that this occurrence takes part in, so "joined by operator and" is not a false statement, and the Role still tells this occurrence apart from the LHS occurrence (id 3) on the same line.

review.notes:
All 48 entries check out against the rulebook and the source (E:/jobs/ff/test/Prepoison_subset/bahavioral_patterns_of_assets/data/RTL_data/neorv32_trng.vhd, lines 380-477). Every entry's line number and line_text match the source exactly.

Tag checks that needed the disambiguation rules, all of which the annotator got right:
- line 416 `sreg <= sreg(sreg'left-1 downto 0) & en_i;`: target sreg = LHS_PROC alone; the slice = RHS_OPERAND + PART_SELECT (joined by `&`, so a primary matches and PART_SELECT is added, per CONFLICT_RULES "PART_SELECT is recorded together with the primary SITE of the occurrence where one matches"); `sreg'left` = ATTR_PREFIX alone.
- line 458 `inv_in(NUM_INV-1 downto 1) <= latch(NUM_INV-2 downto 0);`: the right-hand slice is PART_SELECT alone ("A slice that is the whole right-hand side of a signal assignment matches no primary SITE ... PART_SELECT is written alone there"), while the target slice correctly keeps LHS_CONC + PART_SELECT (the target is the name written before its parentheses).
- line 435 conditional assignment: latch(i) target = LHS_CONC + INDEXED_NAME; second latch(i) = WHEN_EXPR + INDEXED_NAME; sreg(i) = WHEN_COND + INDEXED_NAME; en_i = WHEN_COND; inv_out(i) = WHEN_EXPR + INDEXED_NAME. Chosen/alternative/condition are correctly separated.
- lines 421, 457, 475: an indexed name that is the whole right-hand side gets INDEXED_NAME alone, per the DIRR_ASS exclusion "an index makes it INDEXED_NAME ... written alone where no primary SITE matches".
- lines 440 vs 449: the same statement text is correctly called concurrent (inside the if-generate) and sequential (inside the process), giving LHS_CONC vs LHS_PROC for inv_out(i).
- clk_i/rstn_i: PROCESS_TRIG on the three header lines, EDGE_CHECK for rising_edge(clk_i) at 415/448/469, IF_COND for (rstn_i = '0') at 413/467 — the sensitivity-list / edge / plain-condition three-way split is clean.

Two judgment calls I deliberately did not report as defects:
1. `sreg'left-1` inside the slice range on line 416 is tagged ATTR_PREFIX alone rather than ATTR_PREFIX + RHS_OPERAND. The ATTR_PREFIX context ("The attribute gives a value about the element ... that value, not the element, is what the surrounding expression uses") and section F rule 15 ("The element itself must satisfy the SITE's rule") support the attribute value, not the element, being the operand. This also matches how the annotator treated `sreg'left` and `latch'left` inside index parentheses, where the INDEX exclusion is explicit.
2. Roles on ids sreg-6, latch-4 and sync-5 say the indexed name "forms the whole right-hand side" / "on the right-hand side". That is a true syntactic statement and the Role names the index in the same sentence, so it does not imply DIRR_ASS, whose trigger requires "no index".

No Role holds a line number (all parenthesised numbers such as sync(0), sync(1), inv_in(0), NUM_INV-1 are code text), and no Role uses a purpose word.

All 155 entries in cache_a.json were checked line by line against E:/jobs/ff/test/Prepoison_subset/bahavioral_patterns_of_assets/data/RTL_data/neorv32_cache.vhd lines 27-312.

SITE tags: no defect found. Every primary tag matches its rulebook trigger (DECL_PORT lines 35-40; DECL_SIGNAL line 84; PROCESS_TRIG lines 114 and 133; EDGE_CHECK line 125; IF_COND for the non-edge if/elsif conditions on 116, 168, 170, 171, 172, 190, 199, 210, 243; LHS_PROC for every assignment target inside the two process blocks; DIRR_ASS on 149, 151, 159, 194, 209, 236; RHS_OPERAND on 137, 138, 242; ASSOC_ACTUAL on 280, 281, 283, 284, 285). Add-ons are correct too: FIELD_USE is written alone on every record base at <base>.<field>, including the port-map actuals on 283-290; PART_SELECT is written with IF_COND at line 171 and alone at lines 180 and 181, matching the owner's decision that a slice which is the whole right-hand side gets PART_SELECT alone. No INDEX / INDEXED_NAME / ATTR_PREFIX case exists in this range, and the concatenations on 225/227/235/238 contain only ctrl fields, which are outside this chunk's element list.

Roles: no Role holds a line number, none names a purpose (the mentions of S_LOOKUP, S_CLEAR, S_DOWNLOAD_REQ, S_DOWNLOAD_RSP and S_DOWNLOAD_DONE are the case choices as written, which is syntax), and the pairs that share a line are told apart (host_req_i ids 11 and 12 both on line 172 name amo and debug respectively). The 16 findings are all one kind of omission: 15 DECL_FIELD Roles on lines 39 and 40 do not say whether the record type is declared in this source or outside it (the 15 DECL_FIELD Roles on lines 37, 38 and 84 do say it), and one PART_SELECT Role on line 181 does not give the range selected.

verdicts.corrected_expected: Role "FIELD_USE: reaches field data." is acceptable as written; no correction needed.
verdicts.reason: The reviewer's section G quote exists verbatim, but a more specific rule governs a FIELD_USE occurrence on a record base and it is satisfied. Section F rule 13 (RECORD BASE AND RECORD FIELD) says: "In the base's profile, the occurrence is FIELD_USE. Write one entry for each field reached, and name the field reached in the Role. What the occurrence does belongs to the field." The rulebook's FIELD_USE rule repeats this in its context ("this site records on the base that one of its fields was reached, and which field. Name the field reached in the Role") and in its exclusion ("The SITE for what the occurrence does goes in the field's own entry") and basis ("What the occurrence does there belongs to the field"). Section G's own FIELD_USE bullet is only "FIELD_USE: name the field reached". So for the base at line 156 the required detail is the field name, which the Role gives. The statement and the element's position in it are recorded where the rules put them: entry cache_i.data id 2 at line 156 reads "Whole right-hand side of a sequential signal assignment (the RHS is exactly the field)". No disambiguation rule forces more either: section G only requires the Role to tell occurrences apart "[w]here the same element occurs more than once on a line", and cache_i occurs once on line 156. That ids 4, 5 and 6 also name their statement is a style habit of the annotator, not a rule the rulebook states. Section M CHECK 13 likewise asks only that the base have FIELD_USE and the field have the SITEs for what the occurrence does.

verdicts.corrected_expected: Role: "Target of a sequential signal assignment inside a process (assigned S_IDLE in the others branch)." — no change required.
verdicts.reason: The quoted section D definitions do exist (annotate_rules.md lines 130-141), but they fix the vocabulary of the Structure field (the kinds a Structure lists), not the wording of the Role. Section G only requires the Role to name the statement (sequential signal assignment), the element's position in it (target), and to tell occurrences on the same line apart; it never requires the enclosing structure to be named, let alone named with the Structure kind word. The Role's facts are all true of line 265: it is the target of a sequential signal assignment inside the process, the value assigned is S_IDLE, and the enclosing case choice is others. Moreover the documents themselves use "branch" as the generic word covering case alternatives: rulebook.json LHS_PROC context says "The Structure lists every branch and case alternative that encloses the statement ... This site does not say which kind of branch it is", and the rulebook edit_note records "case alternatives taught as branches". So "the others branch" is not a wrong fact under these sources, and the Role states no purpose (no reset/default/state-machine wording).

verdicts.corrected_expected: Role: "FIELD_USE: reaches field state assigned S_IDLE in the others branch (left-hand side of an assignment)." — no change required.
verdicts.reason: Same basis as id 17. The entry is the record base ctrl_nxt written ctrl_nxt.state, tagged FIELD_USE alone, and section G requires only that FIELD_USE name the field reached; the Role names field state. Section D's "branch" definition constrains the Structure field (checked by code, not given here), not Role wording, and the rulebook uses "branch" generically for case alternatives ("every branch and case alternative", "which kind of branch it is"; edit_note: "case alternatives taught as branches"). The statement of fact — field state assigned S_IDLE on the left-hand side of an assignment under the others choice — is true of line 265, so there is no wrong fact and no purpose word.

verdicts.corrected_expected: Role should name the inner if condition without the false enclosure claim, e.g. "appears in the inner if condition (clr_i = '1'), inside the branch opened by the edge condition on clk_i." Line 380 lies in the branch opened by rising_edge(clk_i) (379 to 387), not in the branch opened by (rstn_i = '0'), which is 376 to 378.
verdicts.reason: Section D defines a branch as running from its if, elsif or else line to the last shown line before the next elsif, else or end if, and says verbatim that a branch never includes the elsif or else line that starts the next branch. Reading the source, 376 opens the (rstn_i = '0') branch, which holds only 377 and 378 and ends at the elsif on 379. Line 380 is therefore inside the elsif branch opened by rising_edge(clk_i), so the Role's statement that it is inside the branch that checks rstn_i = '0' is a wrong fact. The same wording is used correctly at valid_mem id 2 on line 377, so the phrase does mean the branch, not the whole if statement.

The quoted rule "Do not describe behavior that the tag does not need." does exist in section G, but the reported category is role_purpose_word and no purpose word is present: the Role never says what the signal or the branch is for (no reset, clock, enable, initialization, defaults, handshake, bypass, valid flag, state machine). "assigns the read value" only restates the assignment and the indexed read written on the same line; it is the same register as "the array is read with an index" and "supplies the array position", used across this file for analogous occurrences. The Role gives the statement (sequential signal assignment), the element's position (target) as section G requires, holds no line number, and tells this occurrence apart from id 2 on line 378. No section M check is violated, so the entry stands.
